exercise_group.instruction: Let each matrix in Exercises 1–6 act on $$\mathbb{C}^{2}$$ . Find the eigenvalues and a basis for each eigenspace in $$\mathbb{C}^{2}$$ .

In Exercises 7–12, use Example 6 to list the eigenvalues of $$A$$ . In each case, the transformation $$\textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x}$$ is the composition of a rotation and a scaling. Give the angle $$\varphi$$ of the rotation, where $$- \pi < \varphi \leq \pi$$ , and give the scale factor $$r$$ .

In Exercises 13–20, find an invertible matrix $$P$$ and a matrix $$C$$ of the form $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} a & {- b} \\ b & a \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ such that the given matrix has the form $$A = PCP^{- 1}$$ . For Exercises 13–16, use information from Exercises 1–4.

problem.paragraph: In Example 2, solve the first equation in (2) for $$x_{2}$$ in terms of $$x_{1}$$ , and from that produce the eigenvector $$\textbf{y} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 2 \\ {- 1 + 2i} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ for the matrix $$A$$ . Show that this $$\textbf{y}$$ is a (complex) multiple of the vector $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ used in Example 2.

Let $$A$$ be a complex (or real) $$n \times n$$ matrix, and let $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$\mathbb{C}^{n}$$ be an eigenvector corresponding to an eigenvalue $$\text{λ}$$ in $$\mathbb{C}$$ . Show that for each nonzero complex scalar $$\mu$$ , the vector $$\mu\textbf{x}$$ is an eigenvector of $$A$$ .

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 23–26, $$A$$ is a $$2 \times 2$$ matrix with real entries, and $$\textbf{x}$$ is a vector in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ . Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The matrix $$A$$ can have one real and one complex eigenvalue.
(T/F) The points $$A\textbf{x},A^{2}\textbf{x},A^{3}\textbf{x},\ldots$$ always lie on the same circle.
(T/F) The matrix $$A$$ always has two eigenvalues, but sometimes they have algebraic multiplicity $$2$$ or are complex numbers.
(T/F) If the matrix $$A$$ has two complex eigenvalues, then it also has two linearly independent real eigenvectors.

exercise_group.instruction: Chapter 7 will focus on matrices $$A$$ with the property that $$A^{T} = A$$ . Exercises 27 and 28 show that every eigenvalue of such a matrix is necessarily real.

problem.paragraph: Let $$A$$ be an $$n \times n$$ real matrix with the property that $$A^{T} = A$$ , let $$\textbf{x}$$ be any vector in $$\mathbb{C}^{n}$$ , and let $$q = {\overset{‾}{\textbf{x}}}^{T} A\textbf{x}$$ . The equalities below show that $$q$$ is a real number by verifying that $$\overset{‾}{q} = q$$ . Give a reason for each step.

exercise_group.instruction: $$\overline{q} = \overline{\overline{x}^{T} A X} = x^{T} \bar{A x} = x^{T} \bar{A x} = \left(x^{T} \bar{A x}\right)^{T} = \left(\bar{x}\right)^{T} A^{T} x = q \left(a\right) \left(b\right) \left(c\right) \left(d\right) \left(e\right)$$

problem.paragraph: Let $$A$$ be an $$n \times n$$ real matrix with the property that $$A^{T} = A$$ . Show that if $$A\textbf{x} = \text{λ} \textbf{x}$$ for some nonzero vector $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$\mathbb{C}^{n}$$ , then, in fact, $$\text{λ}$$ is real and the real part of $$\textbf{x}$$ is an eigenvector of $$A$$ . [Hint: Compute $${\overset{‾}{\textbf{x}}}^{T} A\textbf{x}$$ , and use Exercise 27. Also, examine the real and imaginary parts of $$A\textbf{x}$$ .]

Let $$A$$ be a real $$n \times n$$ matrix, and let $$\textbf{x}$$ be a vector in $$\mathbb{C}^{n}$$ . Show that $$\text{Re} \left( A\textbf{x} \right) = A\left( \text{Re} \textbf{x} \right)$$ and $$\text{Im} \left( A\textbf{x} \right) = A\left( \text{Im} \textbf{x} \right)$$ .
Let $$A$$ be a real $$2 \times 2$$ matrix with a complex eigenvalue $$\text{λ} = a - bi$$ ( $$b \neq 0$$ ) and an associated eigenvector $$\mathbf{v}$$ in $$\mathbb{C}^{2}$$ .

list.item: Show that $$A \text{(Re} \textbf{v}) = a \text{Re} \textbf{v} + b \text{Im} \textbf{v}$$ and $$A \text{(Im} \textbf{v}) = - b \text{Re} \textbf{v} + a \text{Im} \textbf{v}$$ . [Hint: Write $$\textbf{v} = \text{Re} \textbf{v} + i \text{Im} \textbf{v}$$ , and compute $$A\textbf{v}$$ .]
Verify that if $$P$$ and $$C$$ are given as in Theorem 9, then $$A P = PC$$ .

exercise_group.instruction: [T] In Exercises 31 and 32, find a factorization of the given matrix $$A$$ in the form $$A = PCP^{- 1}$$ , where $$C$$ is a block-diagonal matrix with $$2 \times 2$$ blocks of the form shown in Example 6. (For each conjugate pair of eigenvalues, use the real and imaginary parts of one eigenvector in $$\mathbb{C}^{4}$$ to create two columns of $$P$$ .)
